intro.title: useToggle
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom Angular hook called 'useToggle' to manage a boolean state that can be switched between true and false. You will learn how to encapsulate state logic into a reusable function using Angular's built-in APIs like useState and useCallback. The main technologies involved are Angular hooks, TypeScript for type safety, and functional components. By the end, you'll understand how to create and use custom hooks to simplify state management in your Angular applications.
intro.usecase: The useToggle pattern is fundamental for managing binary UI states in real applications. You'll use it to control visibility of modals, expand/collapse panels in dashboards, toggle between light/dark themes, and switch form fields between edit/view modes. In e-commerce sites, it powers product filter toggles (like 'In Stock Only'), while in admin panels it controls sidebar menus and detail view expansions. Every interactive element with an on/off, show/hide, or expand/collapse behavior relies on this toggle logic.
